action_needed: Dédalo prereleases are now published releases — from 7.0.0-beta.7 on, each beta is a fixed, signed version you can install and update.
The Docker and Trial installer installs the image of its own release — `7.0.0-beta.7` for a beta — and a stack built from an earlier beta needs `--skip-version-check` once on its next image update.

entries.title: The change history of a password field no longer shows the stored password hash.
The hidden 'Calm Scholarly' design preview is removed.
Image quality selector now appears only on hover or on an active component; touch screens keep it visible.
Opening a rich-text field no longer downloads the editor on the first click.
CSV import guesses the target section from more file names and remembers your correction.
The Import files tool's options panel reads as three clear blocks, and the import button stays in reach.
The inspector's Data box keeps its size when you select another component, and you can resize it.
A relation table is framed, with no rules between its column titles
Time machine tool list on phone renders as one card per version
On a phone, the time machine marks the picked version across the whole row and brings its preview into view.
On a phone, the time machine's two version panels, its Apply action and its page counter now stack into one readable column.
Checkboxes and radio buttons fill with a deeper orange so the white tick shows in every browser

The date field's calendar now writes the dates the catalogue actually stores — including year-only, year+month and BCE (negative) years — with localized month names and full keyboard and touch support.
The profile permission tree can be filtered by name or tipo.
The address bar now names the open record, so an edit page can be copied and reopened
The image vector editor now supports undo and redo
The inspector shows again who created, last modified and published a record, and when.
Export: columns are added and reordered by tap on a phone
On a phone, a drilled search field level shows its path
On a phone, moving between search field levels now slides
The autocomplete result list no longer opens as a blank band
component_iri edit row lays out on one aligned line
A read-only field's value starts under its own label again
Rich-text fields in a language with no bundled editor translation now open in English instead of not opening at all.
Change history no longer fails, and restore no longer writes a broken value, when an old history entry holds a malformed link value.
Image derivatives are encoded at full quality again — sharper web and list images, and somewhat larger files
Deleting an image's last file now clears its vector drawing, so a new upload starts fresh
An image uploaded in a format the browser cannot show (TIFF, PSD, PNG…) keeps its full-resolution original AND regains the viewable copy, so the "original" quality is selectable again
The propagate tool on a Project filter now offers the same options as the component.
An image's drawing envelope is removed with the record's last file, not with one quality
Turning pages in *Latest changes* no longer fails with a permission error for users who are not administrators.
The image vector editor now deletes shapes and layers reliably
Saving a drawing in the image vector editor keeps the image visible
The acquisition tools no longer start an import while a new Preview is loading
Remove background works again in the image rotation tool.
Unpublishing every record of an RDF, XML or Markdown publication now also removes its combined file and ZIP
A refused side panel no longer takes over the whole page.
The References panel and its graph open for every user who can read the record, and their page counts add up
Users who are allowed to see a section's change history can open *Latest changes* and *Component history* again.
The acquisition tools no longer let you start a second import while the first one's outcome is unknown
The acquisition tools no longer go silent when a job's progress is lost, and the move panels show a refused run.
The acquisition tools show why a preview or an import failed, instead of "Done."
The selected field is fully tinted in a light orange — its list surfaces included — and its label stays readable in both themes.
A record restored from an archive no longer shows the history of a deleted record that had the same id.
The assistant's find-or-create no longer duplicates a record under concurrent calls
The "Report a problem" tab only appears for users whose profile grants the error-report tool.
Stopping a background export now stops it at once, even while its record selection is still being computed.
The acquisition tools and move panels no longer re-enable an action when the server did not confirm whether the job started.
Pasting into the search panel's Id field adds to what is already there instead of replacing it.
The reference picker of a text area separates the term and its thesaurus part (… | …), instead of gluing them.
A text area reference can link the same term from several references, and deleting a reused reference keeps the others linked.
Update cache never overwrites an edit saved while it runs
Translatable fields in tool forms show the value in your data language, not always in Spanish
Clicking a field puts the cursor in it, every time
Turning a list page no longer jumps the layout
Search: the drag-a-field slot is the same height as the field cards beside it
Thesaurus lists are sorted by name in the reader's language.
Selected text is visibly highlighted in every field, active or not
Opening a record by link no longer lands on a one-row list.
Inspector history panels read as blocks on a phone or tablet
The Section id search field fills its card like every other search field.
Orange warning buttons are readable — white text on a deeper orange in the light theme.
Dark mode: the page canvas no longer sits above the cards, and empty-field hints are legible
Tool Export — the presets panel no longer shows a blank band between its header and the presets.
Plain-text filter values join terms with ', ' when the section map defines no separator
List headers stay readable in Safari, even when rows have different heights
The line under a list row is unbroken across empty columns
Mosaic hover: the record id is no longer cut off, and the publication switch is centred
A portal row's edit cell now fills the row, like its trash cell.
The date field's calendar button is a full-size tap target and no longer covers the field label
The Import files tool's options panel lines up on a phone
Ontology and thesaurus search: the result highlight and the loading state are now in sync.
Search on a phone: the fields panel's level header is as easy to tap as the fields themselves
On a phone, the section list buttons and their show/hide arrow no longer overlap or jump around.
Tools on a phone use the phone's own spacing and header height; only part of the phone adjustments were reaching the screen.
The Update cache tool reads properly on a phone: one component per row, its options and model under it, all lined up.
Upload buttons keep a clear gap between their icon and their label on a phone
Each file in the upload queue is a card, so you can see where one file ends and the next begins
Uploaded-file rows stack on a phone instead of running off the side
The upload queue's "select all" checkbox says what it does again
The search panel keeps the values you typed when the page reloads.
The autocomplete options panel no longer clips its section list
Search option tooltips are legible in dark mode.
The Tools menu in a section list opens its tools again on a phone.
Names and values typed by one user can no longer run script in another user's browser
Server hardening from the CodeQL review — the tag-badge address refuses over-long requests, rich text keeps only raster-image `data:` links, and literal `<` text is no longer turned into `<`.
Third-party packages updated to their latest stable releases, closing every known advisory against them.
SQL the engine runs through psql no longer appears on the psql command line
A user can only assign a record to projects they belong to
Site builder: a Claude Code turn turns off its auto-updater and telemetry in every confinement mode, not only when confined
Site builder: `provision remove` and `provision adopt` can no longer be hung by a pipe planted at a turn HOME's `.gitconfig`, a site's `site.json` or an instance marker
Outbound fetches judge an IPv6 address through every NAT64 prefix that holds it, so nested prefixes cannot reach an internal address.
Bun no longer fetches packages by name outside the lockfile.
A local certificate authority can now only certify the install's own addresses, and its site certificate can be renewed without touching the staff computers.
Ontology files move out of the code tree by default
The installer field *Database role* is now *Database user*.
Dédalo prereleases are now published releases — from 7.0.0-beta.7 on, each beta is a fixed, signed version you can install and update.
The Docker and Trial installer installs the image of its own release — `7.0.0-beta.7` for a beta — and a stack built from an earlier beta needs `--skip-version-check` once on its next image update.
A prerelease build now calls itself by its tag (`7.0.0-beta.7`), and its data version is published beside it.
The profile tool-permissions panel explains each tool — an info button unfolds its description.
"A code server can publish a prerelease (`Build prerelease`), and a published release is never rebuilt."
"Code updates move between prereleases of one version: beta to later beta, beta to its release."
"Prereleases have an official image: `:7.0.1-beta.2`, signed, and never under a release's tag."
"The update panel can ask for prereleases: choose published releases, prereleases or developer builds."
The production installer can now make a local certificate authority, for an intranet with no public name.
Aborting an install (`--abort`) no longer fails with a deadlock when something else is connected to its database.
The installer no longer crashes when a check's helper process stops before reading its request.
A maintenance job whose progress cannot be followed now says so instead of waiting forever.
The publication host's `install.sh` no longer hangs on a stalled Bun download.
Installing or resetting a thesaurus no longer waits without limit behind another session's lock
The publication-marker index is now repaired every 10 minutes as well as at startup, and a repair held off by a running publication is retried instead of skipped.
A running move execute in Maintenance can no longer be hidden by a new Preview
The publication host installer never puts a cut-off file in place on a full disk
An archive restore refuses an ontology node another writer created between the plan and the write
An archive restore no longer plants ontology definitions that the next ontology rebuild would delete
A backup's verification proof now survives a power cut, and a backup is reported done only once its name is safely on disk.
Code updates of a git-checkout install no longer refuse over `.claude` and `CLAUDE.md`
An update or a move transform that committed after a lost connection says what did not run
An export's record selection now respects the database statement ceiling.
A lookup in an external catalogue now always ends within its timeout, even when the name server or the answer stalls.
Exporting a thesaurus never leaves or certifies a partial dump
Installer and container fixes — `--abort` removals survive a power cut, a half-imported thesaurus is no longer reported installed, the published client never points at a missing copy
The installer's configuration and the published client now survive a power cut
The temporary audio copy made for on-premise transcription is deleted as soon as it has been sent.
Interrupted exports and transcriptions no longer leave temporary files behind
Deleting or restoring an ontology record now removes or restores its runtime node.
Building the ontology recovery file no longer stops the server when the disk is full, and the file survives a power cut
The ontology status panel reports a TLD shown under the wrong typology, and the hierarchy typology groups are filed where the master ontology files them
The installer's downloaded ontology files survive a power cut
An ontology update now removes the nodes a new package no longer carries.
Phantom-language removal and the public-tier reconcile no longer hang on a busy publication target
A publication run or unpublish no longer waits without limit on a lock held outside Dédalo
The Reconcile panel offers *Apply* only where you can apply, and a refusal no longer replaces the page
New installations and imported thesauri store record references in their final form
Installing or resetting a thesaurus takes effect at once and no longer needs gigabytes of memory
Time machine restores respect every record's projects and every field's permission; the ontology recovery file is built one at a time
Restoring a whole record from the time machine needs permission on every field it changes; a failed ontology re-index after an update no longer brings the old ontology back
Unpublished media stays unpublished after a power cut — and is never reported withdrawn while it is still served
Rebuilding or updating one user's activity statistics never counts a day twice
Docker stacks — ontology update no longer fails with EACCES
The installer says what to do when the checkout's dependencies are missing.
A code update that is refused says so once, not three times
The component lock requests refuse a section that is not an ontology tipo.
"Build database version: the install-seed build's answer and panel values are documented"
A developer install gets its own unix socket, named after its entity, and is refused while another server holds it.
"`page_globals` now says what kind of build is running (`release_kind`), and the harvesting user agent names the release."
A developer install is reported complete only once `bun run dev` has served, and it ends by saying where to open it.
A developer install now issues the development listener's HTTPS certificate and makes this machine trust it; `bun run tls:renew` and `bun run tls:untrust` manage it afterwards.
The ontology tool's "set records" can no longer write a node into another TLD's namespace.
A developer install now installs the development dependencies `bun run dev` needs, and the development listener can serve HTTPS (`SERVER_TCP_TLS_CERT_FILE` + `SERVER_TCP_TLS_KEY_FILE`).
A developer install now writes a development listener, so `bun run dev` serves the browser on port 3500.
